door_refusals.why: your own words contain number(s) ['3,'] — a number must come from the document, in digits or in words
moves: '3' is written exactly so in the document (e.g. p1.L40): if that is what you mean (a name like this, or that value), quote it: {"quote": "3", "atom": "p1.L40"} — never shorten it
move each number into a quote run: {"quote": "<exact characters>", "atom": "<id>"}
or compute it in a sql run (counts, sums, conversions)
or say it without a number ("several", "a", "each")

door_refusals.why: the text "'%.2f'" puts digits into the value "PRINTF('%.2f', CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(a.text, '([0-9]+\\.[0-9]+)', 1) AS DOUBLE) - CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(b.text, '([0-9]+\\.[0-9]+)', 1) AS DOUBLE)) AS diff" — a value may only carry numbers read from atoms
moves: read the number from the atom that holds it (e.g. regexp_extract over its text) instead of typing it
for a unit factor or physical constant, read it from consts: (SELECT value FROM consts WHERE id = 'K.per_kilo')
0, 1 and 100 are allowed as written; constants in WHERE/ON (choosing) are always allowed
